findings.description: pipeline_list view had no @login_required, unlike sibling leasing_list, causing a 500 (AnonymousUser filter TypeError) instead of a redirect for unauthenticated access
tests/acceptance/test_leasing.py hardcoded a stale route (/leasing/list/) that had never executed under --collect-only

Implemented Phase A of docs/TOP_01_PLAN.md: A-2 (BDD suite over real HTTP via live_server), A-3 (acceptance suite runs pre-merge via live_server fallback), A-4 (real 10-minute build-time budget on docker-publish.yml), A-5 (schema-based response validation for all tests/acceptance/*.py files). A-1 was already done.

PR #322 (fix/security-lint-and-mypy-config) introduced pytest.ini testpaths + a baked-in addopts -k filter (including "not acceptance") so a bare pytest invocation is safe-by-default. The acceptance-check CI job had no counter -k override, so it silently inherited the exclusion: 41 acceptance tests deselected, 0 collected, hard CI failure.

The pytest.ini change itself was a deliberate, valuable security remediation (Finding 4) and was NOT reverted; fixed by adding an explicit -k "" override to acceptance-check pytest invocation in ci-quality.yml, relying on last-value-wins CLI-vs-ini precedence for the store-type -k option.

Branch was behind main (missing Phase A/PR #323 fixes: acceptance-check real-run + collectstatic, scoped collection hook). Merged origin/main in first; resolved a genuine .pre-commit-config.yaml conflict by keeping this branch tightened mypy args/deps (this PR actual point) plus main tests/acceptance/ mypy exclude, and unioning both name-tests-test exclude patterns. Verified mypy still passes clean (315 files) with the tightened config before pushing.
